findings.claim: the r2 test asserts the new install URL appears in plugin.HOOK_COMMAND once, so it passes if one of the hook's two install lines still names the old repository; r1 does not catch that either, because src/kmctl/plugin.py is allowed to name the old repository
commands.md says patch refuses the string entry JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm#…, but _names_old_package now also refuses the string JasperHG90/kmctl/apm#…; the page should name both

verdict.text: The rename is complete and correct.
Everything kmctl points users at names JasperHG90/kmctl.
Installs from the old name are still recognised in every case the plan names, and each refusal names the right `apm uninstall`.
The release script no longer moves the v0.3.0 example.
All gates and the four eval rows are green on a fresh stamp.
Two non-blocking findings remain: one test should be stronger, and one doc sentence is incomplete.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests and integration pass; rows r1 to r4 pass; stamp green 4f03fd0a54a78e03de43e164c1047ae66d95f421dfd6459d54ba18f701471b1f.
Read the whole diff and the changed functions in src/kmctl/plugin.py: `_repo_of`, `_old_layout`, `_names_old_package`, `_old_entry`, `patch` and `uninstall_name`.
The refusal for each case: String entry from either name: uninstall names the entry as written, minus `#ref`.
v0.3.0 lock with a dict entry: `uninstall_name` builds it from the entry's own URL, so `github.com/<name>/apm` with its case kept.
v0.3.0 lock with no entry: the canonically cased `<repo>/apm` of the repository the lock names.
A dict entry from the old URL with the new layout is not refused, and `kmctl_package` still finds it by name and path, as the plan intends.
`_repo_of` checks REPO first; the old name does not contain the new one, so the order is safe.
Eval tests: r1 runs git ls-files and allows only plugin.py, tests and the two docs pages, with a negative lookahead for `/apm`.
r3 is parametrised over both names for the string entry, the v0.3.0 lock with an entry, and the v0.3.0 lock alone, and asserts exit 1 plus the exact uninstall text.
r4 runs set_version on a copy and checks the example survives.
The `-k` filters select the intended tests.
Grepped tracked files outside .okf/decisions and .loop for the old name.
The only hits are plugin.py, tests, the how-to's Older installs example and commands.md's refusal description.
The apm/antigravity hooks name no repository, which matches the re-signed r2.
/home/vscode/kmctl-starter: commit 8ec63a6 renames the repository there, and its tracked files no longer name the old one.
release.py: the `pin_apm_doc` removal is clean, and the module and `set_version` docstrings match the new behaviour.
f1 (test-strength, non-blocking, row r2): `assert install in plugin.HOOK_COMMAND` is satisfied by either of the two install lines in the hook.
Add an assertion that HOOK_COMMAND does not contain OLD_REPO, or count two occurrences.
The code itself is correct.
f2 (docs, non-blocking): after this change, `_names_old_package` treats a string entry from either repository name as the old form.
docs/reference/commands.md step 1 still names only `JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm#…`.
Mention `JasperHG90/kmctl/apm#…` too, or say "the string form of either name".
`_repo_of` matches by substring, so `jasperhg90/kmctl-starter` would count as kmctl in a dict entry's git URL or in a lock repo_url.
That only matters when the lock has `virtual_path: plugin` for that repository, which kmctl-starter never has.
The old check had the same substring behaviour.
This is not a finding.
